summary: The study describes the fabrication of W/Al2O3 superlattices on flexible polymer substrates using atomic layer deposition (ALD) to achieve high X-ray reflectivity. The ALD process involves sequential surface reactions with gas precursors to deposit conformal and ultrasmooth thin films. The process was optimized for flexible substrates by reducing the growth temperature to 125 °C to prevent damage to the polymer substrates. The resulting W/Al2O3 superlattices exhibit high X-ray reflectivity and are suitable for applications in X-ray mirrors.
evidence: Atomic layer deposition (ALD) techniques were used to fabricate W/Al2O3 superlattices with high X-ray reflectivity on flexible Kapton® polyimide and polyethylene naphthalate (PEN) polymer substrates. The ALD of W/Al2O3 nanolaminates has also been demonstrated on polysilicon micromirrors and carbon nanotubes. In this work, the growth temperature was reduced to 125 °C to avoid damaging the polymer substrates. W ALD growth was also performed at 125 °C using tungsten hexafluoride, WF6, and disilane, Si2H6. The ALD W/Al2O3 nanolaminate growth was performed in a viscous flow ALD reactor operating at a N2 carrier gas pressure of ∼133 Pa. The excellent X-ray reflectivity on the polymeric substrates is attributed to the precise bilayer thicknesses obtained by ALD processing.
